limits: This supplement revisits previously excluded leads and runs fresh news-led searches for all 13 ballot justices, with no date cutoff. It is a bounded discovery pass, not an inventory of every unpublished opinion.

News coverage, judicial profiles, legal reporting and commentary supply leads. Official court PDFs and earlier official docket checks supply identity, publication and participation evidence; third-party case indexes are discovery aids only.

All Supreme Court opinions are published under rule 8.1105(a). Review votes and separate review-stage statements are distinct actions and do not establish participation in an underlying Court of Appeal opinion.
A decision is counted once; each ballot justice has one participation row, even if that justice both joins the court opinion and writes separately. Assigned participation is included when verified.

An old nonpub PDF may survive a later publication order. SK Trading was moved to the incidental published list after the later official certification was found. Each record retains its version checks and remaining uncertainties; this is not a complete current-authority audit.
Depublished and withdrawn records are retained separately as historical records, not added to the ordinary unpublished totals. An unsigned or unidentified role is never inferred from news alone.
Broad legal tags were assigned from selected opinion passages and remain provisional. Summary completion is tracked separately and does not imply a justice supported a particular policy outcome.

Search counts record the searches actually performed. Official-document retrieval is verification work. The coverage table gives each stop reason, including structural limits for Supreme Court justices.

No result for a justice means none was verified within this search scope; it does not mean that justice participated in no unpublished cases. News selection is not a measure of workload or judicial quality.

Original catalog and summary files remain unchanged. Verified new unpublished summaries are added to the reader after source checks; docket-only records may remain without summaries. URLs, identifiers and hashes are retained; temporary full-text source files are removed after review.
